title: Rate coding
summary: The message can be how many spikes fall inside a window.

terms.definition: A code in which the signal is the number of spikes per unit time, not the precise time of each one.

terms.plain: how many spikes in the window
terms.definition: The number of spikes a neuron emits during a chosen interval.
The full list of times at which a neuron fired. A rate is a summary of that list.

cards.text:
A spike train is the list of times a neuron fired.
A rate throws away the individual times and keeps the count.

lines: Spikes at 10 ms, 30 ms, 50 ms, and 90 ms.
The spike count is 4. The rate is 40 per second.

question.prompt: Spikes at 10, 30, 50, and 90 ms. How many spikes are in a 100 ms window?
question.why: Four events fall inside the window. 40 per second is the rate, not the count.
question.simpler: Count the spikes. The rate comes after you divide by time.

question.prompt: A rate code keeps which part of the spike train?
choices: How many spikes fell in the window
The exact time of every spike
question.why: The count is the message. The precise times are discarded.
question.simpler: If the times themselves matter, you are no longer reading a rate.

recall.question: What is a spike train?
recall.answer: The list of times a neuron fired.

deeper.note: Adrian and Zotterman showed a single sensory ending whose impulse frequency rose with the strength of a stretch. The count in a window is the classic rate code.

paper.title: The impulses produced by sensory nerve-endings: Part II. The response of a Single End-Organ
paper.section: Impulse frequency rises with stimulus intensity.
